title: Kerala CM Deadlock Drags On as Congress Factions Clash
excerpt: A week after the UDF's historic win, Rahul Gandhi and Kharge still cannot break a three-way standoff over who leads Kerala.
body:
Congress cannot name Kerala's next Chief Minister — and a marathon Saturday meeting in New Delhi only deepened the impasse. Uncertainty continues over the selection of the next Chief Minister of Kerala despite the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) securing a decisive majority of 102 seats in the 140-member Assembly.

**What happened in Delhi:**
The high-level meeting, held at the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, began at 4 pm and concluded around 7 pm, attended by senior leaders Rahul Gandhi, V. D. Satheesan, K. C. Venugopal, Ramesh Chennithala, and KPCC president Sunny Joseph. AICC observer Deepa Dasmunsi confirmed that while consultations have been completed, the ultimate decision has been deferred to the party High Command, with Rahul Gandhi and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge set to make the final call.

**Why three names, not one:**
AICC General Secretary K. C. Venugopal reportedly enjoys the support of a majority of the 63 Congress MLAs, while outgoing Leader of the Opposition V. D. Satheesan has strong backing from public sentiment and key UDF allies such as the Indian Union Muslim League. Former state Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala's camp is staking its claim on the basis of his seniority and administrative experience. The delay is partly attributed to the central leadership's displeasure over 'poster wars' and public demonstrations by rival factional supporters, with Rahul Gandhi warning that such displays of infighting could damage the party's massive electoral mandate.

**What happens next:**
Congress President Kharge has left for Karnataka, postponing a follow-up meeting with Rahul Gandhi, with party sources now expecting a final decision only after Kharge returns to New Delhi on Monday. A May 23 deadline for government formation adds urgency — the new Chief Minister must be sworn in by then.
nri_angle: Kerala sends the largest share of Indian migrants to the United States, and the state's next Chief Minister will directly shape labour export policy, NRI remittance frameworks, and the welfare programmes that protect Malayali-American families' relatives back home.
author: Diaspora Desk
